rows.grounds: points to that state of identity-union
grounds worship in oneness with the deity
gives the reason: its nature is supreme reflective awareness

items.question: Why is worship already complete in the state of identity-union?
premises: In that state worship occurs through identity-union.
Its nature is supreme reflective awareness.
A resonance arises by itself from that awareness.
items.inference: Therefore worship is already fully present without external ritual.
uncertainties: dhvaniḥ may mean inner resonance, mantra-sound, or spontaneous vibration; the verse leaves the exact mode open.
items.plain_english: There, through union in identity, worship is already complete, because its very nature is supreme reflective awareness, which is the resonance that arises by itself.

rows.grounds: identifies it with the supreme heart
describes its power to dissolve all manifestation

items.question: What is the ever-risen resonance identified as in this teaching?
premises: The resonance is always risen.
That resonance is called the supreme great heart.
In that heart self-reflection melts the entire universe.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme heart is the ever-present self-reflective power that dissolves all manifestation.
uncertainties: drāvitāśeṣaviśvakaḥ can suggest melting, liquefying, or dissolving; the intended nuance is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: That ever-risen resonance is called the supreme great Heart. In that Heart, its own self-reflection melts the entire universe.

rows.grounds: spans the range of experienced states
names this movement as the general spanda
locates the teaching in authoritative text

rows.gloss: whose nature is surging in itself
rows.grounds: defines spanda as self-arising inner surge

items.question: How does the scripture define the general vibration called spanda?
premises: This vibration arises across the range from grasping states onward.
The scripture calls it the general spanda.
Its nature is a surging within the self.
items.inference: Therefore general spanda is the self-surging pulse present throughout ordinary experience.
uncertainties: bhāvagrahādi may refer to grasping of objects, mental states, or both; the scope is compressed.
items.plain_english: The scripture calls that vibration the general spanda, present from the grasping of states onward, and its nature is a surging within the self.

rows.gloss: a slight movement, a non-other shining
rows.grounds: defines the minimal stir as inseparable manifestation
metaphor for the stir in awareness

rows.gloss: of the ocean of awakening, not
rows.grounds: locates the wave in awakened consciousness

items.question: What is the slight movement described as a wave in the ocean of awakening?
premises: The slight movement is a shining not other than consciousness.
This movement is like a wave of the ocean of awakening.
That wave does not exist apart from consciousness.
items.inference: Therefore even the smallest stir of manifestation is inseparable from awakened consciousness.
uncertainties: The compound kiṃciccalanametāvadananyasphuraṇaṃ is compressed; the exact syntactic break is interpretive.
items.plain_english: That slight movement is nothing but a shining not other than consciousness; it is a wave of the ocean of awakening and cannot exist apart from that consciousness.

rows.gloss: the movement of wavelessness and waves itself
rows.grounds: includes both stillness and motion as ocean-activity
the nature of being an ocean

rows.gloss: this is the essence of all
rows.grounds: declares consciousness as the core of everything
characterizes the world as grounded in consciousness
describes the world as seemingly insentient

items.question: What is the true essence of the seemingly inert world?
premises: Ocean-ness consists in movements of both wavelessness and waves.
This same principle is the essence of all.
The inert world has consciousness as its essence.
items.inference: Therefore the world, though appearing inert, is essentially consciousness in varied movement.
uncertainties: nistaraṅgataraṅgādi is metaphorical; whether it maps to specific states of awareness is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Ocean-ness is nothing but the play of stillness and waves, and this is the essence of everything. Even the inert world is, at its core, consciousness.

rows.gloss: because established in dependence on that, having that as essence
rows.grounds: grounds the world's essence in consciousness
names the cosmic sphere of manifestation

items.question: Why is the great Heart said to be the essence of all manifestation?
premises: All things are established in dependence on that consciousness.
Because of that dependence, they have that as their essence.
This existent world, called the egg of Maya, is rooted in Brahma.
items.inference: Therefore the great Heart is the true essence underlying all manifested existence.
uncertainties: brahmamūlaṃ may be read cosmologically or as a pointer to a higher conscious ground; the verse does not fully resolve the level.
items.plain_english: Because everything stands dependent on that, its essence is that great Heart. Thus this existent world, called the egg of Maya, is rooted in Brahma.

rows.gloss: the ascent of will, knowledge, and action
rows.grounds: names the three powers required for manifestation
denies existence apart from these powers
states the condition for being real

rows.gloss: from the ascent of that triad of powers in Bhairava
rows.grounds: grounds existence in the three powers within Bhairava-consciousness

items.question: Under what condition can anything be called truly existent?
premises: Nothing is called existent without the ascent of will, knowledge, and action.
Existence arises from the ascent of that triad of powers.
That ascent occurs in the Bhairava-conscious self.
items.inference: Therefore true existence depends on the activity of the three powers within consciousness.
uncertainties: bhairavīye cidātmani could be taken as a locative description or as a more technical doctrinal designation.
items.plain_english: Nothing can be called truly existent without the ascent of will, knowledge, and action. Such existence arises only from the ascent of that triad of powers in the Bhairava-conscious self.

rows.gloss: that from that outward, or else
rows.grounds: indicates outward projection from the source

rows.gloss: indeed the true-form nature of these
rows.grounds: states the real nature of existent things

rows.gloss: the state of being the triad of powers
rows.grounds: identifies their essence with the three powers

items.question: What is the true nature of things that are emitted into manifestation?
premises: Things are emitted outward from that source.
This emission defines their manifested form.
The true nature of existent things is to be the triad of powers.
items.inference: Therefore manifested realities are not other than the three powers of consciousness.
uncertainties: bahirvātha is slightly ambiguous; it may contrast outward emission with another mode not spelled out here.
items.plain_english: What is emitted outward from that source is indeed emitted as manifestation. Thus the true nature of all existent things is simply their identity with the triad of powers.

rows.grounds: identifies the same reality through phases

rows.gloss: dissolved in the fire of prior awareness

items.question: What happens to outward manifestation when supreme awareness reabsorbs it?
premises: Supreme awareness draws emission back into itself.
The same reality remains through that retraction.
Its outward form is dissolved in the fire of prior awareness.
items.inference: Therefore external manifestation is only a temporary form of the one reality reabsorbed by awareness.
uncertainties: prāgbodha could mean prior, original, or foundational awareness; the temporal nuance is interpretive.
items.plain_english: When supreme awareness draws emission back into itself, that same reality remains, while its outward form is dissolved in the fire of original awareness.

rows.gloss: reduced to the remainder of inner-sound reflection
rows.grounds: describes the subtle residue after dissolution
identifies the final state as spacious selfhood
states the arrival at that condition

rows.gloss: from the range of the triad of powers
rows.grounds: indicates transcendence of the three powers' domain

items.question: What state is reached beyond the range of the three powers?
premises: After dissolution, only the reflection of inner sound remains.
From there a further attainment occurs.
That attainment is sheer void-selfhood beyond the range of the triad of powers.
items.inference: Therefore beyond the domain of the three powers the reality abides as spacious void-selfhood.
uncertainties: khātmatva may suggest voidness, spaciousness, or sky-like selfhood; the verse supports all three shades.
items.plain_english: What remains is reduced to the reflection of inner sound, and from there it fully attains sheer void-selfhood, beyond the range of the triad of powers.

rows.gloss: having reached the nature of pure feeling
rows.grounds: describes the transition into felt awareness
locates the process in the withdrawing self
indicates its role as earlier or foundational
identifies the same heart in creation

items.question: How is the heart of dissolution related to the heart of creation?
premises: Having become pure feeling, this reality dissolves in the self of dissolution.
That is called the heart of dissolution.
The same heart is regarded as foundational in creation.
items.inference: Therefore dissolution and creation share one underlying heart of consciousness.
uncertainties: prācyaṃ can mean prior, eastern, or original; the verse leaves the emphasis open.
items.plain_english: Having become pure feeling, this dissolves in the self of dissolution. That is the heart of dissolution, and in creation it is regarded as the same foundational Heart.

rows.gloss: this reflection on such a form, natural and unobstructed

rows.grounds: identifies that reflection as the sense of I

items.question: What is meant by the natural and unobstructed sense of 'I'?
premises: There is a natural, unobstructed reflection on this reality.
That reflection is called 'I'.
This 'I' is the luminosity of light itself.
items.inference: Therefore the true sense of 'I' is the self-luminosity of consciousness.
uncertainties: etadrūpa may refer to the form just described or to the nature of reality as such; the reference is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: They call that natural, unobstructed reflection 'I'. This is nothing other than the luminosity of consciousness itself.
